source.quote: Hegel's own page for the H200, read 2026-11-24. « Digital inputs »: « 1x Coaxial (RCA) S/PDIF - 24/192, 2x Optical S/PDIF - 24/96, 1x USB B- 24/192, 1x USB A 2.0 - USB Drives (10,000 songs), 1x Network - 24/192 ». « Digital outputs »: « 1x Coaxial S/PDIF - 24/192 ». No DSD figure appears anywhere on the page, and the streaming-formats list contains none. No DAC chip is named anywhere on the page, and no digital filter, oversampling or NOS row exists.

facts.chip: Not named anywhere on the page.

_usb_a_192_et_non_384_sur_ce_modele: « 1x USB B- 24/192 », where the D50, the H400 and the H600 all give USB 32/384. Same brand, same template, and this model's USB receiver stops at 24/192 - level with its own coaxial input. The USB ceiling is a property of the receiver, and this range publishes three different ones.
_une_prise_usb_qui_nest_pas_une_entree_a: « 1x USB A 2.0 - USB Drives (10,000 songs) » sits in the list of digital inputs. It is a port for a memory stick, not an audio input, and the figure beside it is a song count. Nothing is written from it. The row is a reminder that an « input » on a spec sheet is whatever the maker chose to put in that list.
